utilityName: City of Cleburne Backflow Prevention Program
testingFrequency: Upon installation, repair, or relocation; annual thereafter
dueBasis: Cleburne says all backflow protection assemblies must be tested upon installation, repair, or relocation and that all backflow assemblies should be tested annually.
officialListLabel: Find BPAT testers registered to work in Cleburne
penalties: Cleburne says BPAT testers no longer submit paper reports directly to the City; registration and approved-list status are handled through VEPO after credential verification.
sourceExcerpt: Cleburne uses VEPO Envirotrax for online backflow test reports, annual testing context, registered BPAT lookup, and license/insurance/test-accuracy verification.
verdictSummary: Cleburne is a strong VEPO intent page because it explicitly combines annual testing, no-paper report submission, registered BPAT search, and verified tester approval.
whoIsAffected: Cleburne customers with backflow assemblies, annual testing obligations, and fire protection sprinkler assemblies.
residentialNotes: Residential users should confirm whether a device is in Cleburne's assembly record before scheduling.
The registered BPAT route is safer than treating a generic provider as City-approved.
commercialNotes: Commercial and higher-risk assemblies should keep the annual test and Envirotrax submission sequence together.
Fire protection sprinkler systems require the fire-company employment overlay.

annualTesting.summary: Cleburne states all backflow assemblies should be tested annually after installation, repair, or relocation triggers.
highlights: VEPO Envirotrax handles online report submission.
Registered BPAT lookup is linked from the City page.
workflowSteps: Confirm the assembly and annual due status with Cleburne's backflow program.
Use a BPAT registered to work in Cleburne.
Have the tester submit through VEPO Envirotrax instead of paper.

irrigation.summary: Cleburne's cross-connection examples include irrigation, so irrigation users should confirm whether the assembly is tracked and reportable under the same VEPO flow.
highlights: Irrigation is named as a potential backflow source.
Assembly status determines the compliance action.
VEPO reporting remains the report route.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the irrigation system has a reportable assembly.
Submit the result in VEPO Envirotrax.

fireLine.summary: Cleburne states fire protection sprinkler assemblies must be tested or repaired by a BPAT who is a full-time employee of a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
highlights: Fire protection sprinkler assemblies have a separate rule.
State Fire Marshal licensing context matters.
The BPAT still needs the Cleburne/VEPO registration path.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the assembly serves fire protection sprinklers.
Use a BPAT employed by a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
Make sure the Cleburne report is submitted through VEPO.
Use Cleburne's program page to identify the assembly and test trigger.
Select a BPAT registered to work in Cleburne.
Have the tester enter the report in VEPO Envirotrax.
Keep fire sprinkler constraints separate from ordinary domestic or irrigation assemblies.
failureHighlights: Paper reports are not the current Cleburne submission path.
Registration and approval depend on license, insurance, and test accuracy verification.
Fire protection assemblies require a full-time employee of a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.

costBand.pricingNotes: The source-backed cost risk is wasted time from the wrong tester or paper-only submission.
